key_insight: A hybrid framework uses large language models to elicit and formalize expert and stakeholder preferences, then integrates those preferences into constrained optimization to prioritize health-post upgrades that maximize population coverage in Ethiopia.
problem_solved: How to allocate limited resources for upgrading rural health posts so as to maximize access to essential services while systematically incorporating diverse expert and stakeholder preferences and constraints.
method: Use LLMs to elicit, standardize, and encode qualitative expert and stakeholder knowledge (priorities, trade-offs, contextual constraints) into machine-readable preference models.
Combine those encoded preferences with mathematical optimization (coverage-maximization under budget/operational constraints) to generate prioritized upgrade plans and trade-off analyses.
Run scenario and robustness checks to produce interpretable, policy-ready recommendations that reflect stakeholder values and practical constraints.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, repeatable pattern for integrating human expertise into algorithmic planning via LLMs, improving real-world applicability, interpretability, and stakeholder alignment of ML-driven resource-allocation models.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: LLM-based preference elicitation → preference encoding → constrained optimizer → prioritized upgrade map/report
Map of Ethiopia overlayed with existing health posts, candidate upgrades, and population coverage gains
Trade-off chart (e.g., coverage vs. budget or equity) showing alternative priority sets under different stakeholder weightings
Icon set representing stakeholders, constraints, and outcomes (health workers, budgets, distance/coverage, robustness)
paper_title: Health Facility Location in Ethiopia: Leveraging LLMs to Integrate Expert Knowledge into Algorithmic Planning
paper_authors: Yohai Trabelsi, Guojun Xiong, Fentabil Getnet, Stéphane Verguet, Milind Tambe
